claim: Pricing is quote-based, with customized modular packages.
evidence: The page requests use cases and provides a Get a quote action; it publishes no numeric starting price.

claim: Pricing requires a quote; Premium and Enterprise are listed.
evidence: Premium and Enterprise describe feature packages and request a demo/quote rather than listing dollar amounts.

claim: Pinned root license points to documentation/licenses rather than identifying an SPDX license.
evidence: Shared GitHub capture contains one sentence directing readers to documentation/licenses.

claim: Pinned current ResourceSpace core license is BSD-style with a fourth naming/trademark condition; use, modification and redistribution are permitted.
evidence: Current text contains standard BSD redistribution/non-endorsement conditions plus a ResourceSpace naming condition. It is not exact BSD-3-Clause; custom LicenseRef retained. No commercial-use or hosting restriction appears.

claim: No software or per-user charge; only support and hosted storage over 10GB are charged.
locator: Is ResourceSpace really free? / How many users can we add?
evidence: FAQ explicitly identifies support and storage as the only charges and says self-hosting can remain free with no per-user restriction.

claim: First-party cloud hosting is available, including 10GB free.
evidence: ResourceSpace offers free cloud systems and paid packages with installation, configuration, hosting, backups, upgrades and support.

claim: GitHub is official development code; stable release branches remain in SVN.
evidence: Official instructions point to resourcespace/resourcespace on GitHub and say release branches currently exist only in Subversion.

claim: Workflow states/actions and reverting metadata/uploads are available.
locator: Workflow states / Workflow actions / Ready to revert
evidence: States control visibility/editing/actions; admins can edit actions; resource logs permit reverting uploads and metadata.
Pinned shared capture contains GNU GPL version 3 and application licensing notice; official product/download pages also identify GNU GPL v3.

claim: All application interfaces/features and unlimited users are available in the free download.
evidence: Official indexed page explicitly includes all interfaces/functions and unlimited users, with standard and Docker installation options.

claim: First-party Alchemy SaaS hosting and paid services are offered.
evidence: Alchemy describes Phraseanet SaaS on its own hosting infrastructure alongside installation, training and maintenance contracts.

claim: Phraseanet supports metadata extraction, faceted/thesaurus search, validation, galleries, bulk indexing/export and an API; matching SaaS portals and integrations needs validation.
locator: Optimisez / Recherchez / Partagez et publiez / Administrez
evidence: Product page describes batch indexing/export, IPTC/XMP and other metadata, Elasticsearch facets/thesaurus, granular collection/document rights, annotations, validations and galleries. It promotes Parade separately for customized front offices; no automatic migration claim made.

claim: Repository is active, not archived or disabled, with latest release 4.1.25 on 2026-10-21.
evidence: Shared GitHub capture reports current push and 4.1.25 release; rsx reports three active maintainers and five releases in 90 days.

claim: Formal OSI approval of the exact custom ResourceSpace license is not established; a naming condition does not by itself violate the Open Source Definition.
locator: OSI Approved Licenses; compared with https://opensource.org/osd section 4
evidence: The OSI directory lists BSD-3-Clause but no ResourceSpace license. OSI requires formal review for approval; OSD section 4 expressly allows derived works to use different names. U/osi=false is a conservative formal-approval hold rather than a finding of non-open use rights.
